label: copy-phase input w at the first or second recall step (early in the sequence)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input token is w, and only at the first two copy steps after <DEL> (recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the input is original token 0 or 1). It never fires on any other input token, never in the original or delimiter phase, and never at later copy steps. Magnitude: strongest when w is the first original token, fed back right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1; 92% of activation mass, top activations about 3.4-3.5). It is weak (about 0.03-0.2 of max) when w is the second original token (recall_idx 2). It also falls off with sequence length: at recall_idx 1 it is almost always active for L<=7, sometimes for L=8, and essentially never for L=9; at recall_idx 2 it only fires for short sequences (L<=6). The step cap t<=8 approximates this length dependence. Dev split: precision 0.84, recall 0.90, F1 0.87, mass recall 0.98. The core clause (w at recall_idx 1, L<=7) has precision 0.999 and holds 90% of the mass.

issues: The core claims hold. All activation is in the copy phase (original and delimiter phases: 0 active), and in_tok == w accounts for 100% of the mass. Activity occurs only at recall_idx 1 (92.3% of mass) and recall_idx 2 (7.7%). On test, the clause w & recall_idx 1 & L<=7 has precision 0.9999 and mass recall 0.903. The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.835, R 0.900, F1 0.867, mass recall 0.981.

One magnitude claim is wrong in its detail. The explanation says activity falls off with sequence length, but at recall_idx 2 it does not change steadily with L. Dev precision of w & recall_idx 2 by L: L=3 0.00 (468 predicted), L=4 0.47, L=5 0.90, L=6 0.56, L=7 0.05. So recall_idx 2 never fires for L=3 and peaks at L=5. The t<=8 cap includes L=3 recall_idx 2 (t=5), which makes that case a small but systematic false-positive class.
The t<=8 cap cuts out recall_idx 1 at L=8 (t=9), even though that case fires 56% of the time. At recall_idx 1, L=9 is essentially dead (precision 0.02), which matches the explanation.

The remaining false positives at recall_idx 2 for L=4 and L=6 (about 50% precision) do not split cleanly on anything I tried (prev_tok letter/digit/vowel, prev_tok == w, in_count, the next original token being a digit). They look like weak activations (0.03-0.2 of max) hovering near the firing threshold, not a hidden variable.
The missed activations under the refined predicate hold only 0.1% of the mass (e.g. w at recall_idx 2 with L=7, activation 0.01-0.11 of max), which is scattered noise.

A refined predicate (recall_idx 1 with L<=8, or recall_idx 2 with 4<=L<=6) reaches test F1 0.895 (P 0.817, R 0.989, mass recall 0.999), against 0.867 for the recorded predicate. That is a modest gain from fixing detail-level boundaries. The label does not overclaim.
